title: Real-output corpus entry
description: One compact record about a real, owner-reviewed output (AES-V2.6 / SUE-564). Canonical content stays in its own SSOT — this record carries refs, a commit or content hash, and evaluation metadata, never the article or artifact body. additionalProperties is false by design: a field that would carry a body has nowhere to go, so an archive attempt fails schema validation rather than needing a separate detector. `reference_eligible` is a separate judgement from `owner_verdict` — published does not mean reference-quality, and an L1 PASS does not either.

transformation.description: The transformation axis this output demonstrates, e.g. summarize, synthesize, adapt, recreate. Free text — the transformation profile vocabulary is owned by AES-V2.9, not duplicated here.

provenance_class.description: Reuses the vocabulary already pinned by schemas/reference-evaluation.schema.json rather than inventing a second one.

lineage_ref.description: Present when provenance_class is generated_output: identifies the generation lineage (e.g. a Skill/profile/calibration combination) so repeated selection from the same lineage can be detected — see the L1 anti-collapse rule in schemas/l1-review.schema.json.

owner_verdict.description: unknown is the required default when no owner acceptance/rejection has actually been expressed. Never inferred from publication, from an L1 pass, or from silence — see V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §11.

reference_eligible.description: Whether this output is eligible for later selection as a comparison GOOD reference. Published does not automatically mean reference-quality, and an L1 PASS does not either — this is a distinct, explicit judgement and is never derived automatically from owner_verdict or from any pass/fail result.

reference_eligible_rationale.description: Required whenever reference_eligible is true: why this specific output earns eligibility, not merely that it was accepted or passed.

failure_labels.description: Named failure shapes observed, where applicable — e.g. 'source-tour', 'translationese', 'formulaic-voice'. Free text so a new failure shape never requires a schema change.

source_ref.description: A pointer to the canonical content, never a copy of it.

dimensions.description: Which dimensions this output is strong or weak on. Free-text dimension names so the corpus can note a finding before a rubric dimension formally exists for it.
